fix: Keep these as scratch fields on TwoDimensionalViewport (e.g. raw_children: Vec<(ChildVicinity, T, Size, TwoDimensionalConstraints)>, measured_rows: Vec<f32>, measured_columns: Vec<f32>), call clear() and resize() at the start of layout_with_measure_inner, and index the measured extents by (index - row_range.start) / (index - column_range.start) instead of BTreeMap::entry per cell, since the materialized ranges are contiguous. Only the returned children Vec then allocates per layout.

Use the entry API so each cell does one lookup instead of contains_key + insert + get: match self.cache.entry(vicinity) { Entry::Occupied(e) => e.into_mut(), Entry::Vacant(e) => match self.delegate.child_at(vicinity) { Some(c) => e.insert(c), None => continue } }, then clone the child once. self.cache and self.delegate are disjoint fields, so the borrows are fine.

evidence:
let row_extent = extent_at(&self.rows, y_index);
let column_extent = extent_at(&self.columns, x_index);
fix: row_extent depends only on y_index, but it is recomputed (two offset_for_index lookups) for every cell in the inner x loop. Move `let row_extent = extent_at(&self.rows, y_index);` to just after the `for y_index in row_range.clone() {` line and keep only `let column_extent = extent_at(&self.columns, x_index);` inside the inner loop (or precompute column extents once per layout into a scratch buffer).

Change to children.sort_unstable_by(|left, right| match self.main_axis { ... }) with the same comparator. Every child has a unique vicinity (cache is keyed by it and each cell is visited once), so stability is irrelevant, and the stable sort allocates a scratch buffer on every layout for non-trivial lengths. Optionally skip the sort for the Vertical main axis, where the row-major raw order is already the required order.

These panic on values an app author passes to public constructors/setters, and the rustdoc has no # Panics section. Either document the contract (`# Panics` in the doc comments of new, set_axis_directions and set_cache_extent) and add maybe_/try_ forms returning Result (e.g. try_new, try_set_cache_extent) with a typed error, per CONTRIBUTING.md; or return the error from the public API directly. Converting to Result changes the signature, so note it as breaking in the CHANGELOG.
